import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/test_9.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and types
target_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
target_dtypes = {
    'admit': int,
    'gre': int,
    'gpa': float,
    'prestige': int
}

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)  # ignore the first numerical index column
    # Ensure columns are exactly the target columns
    df = df[target_columns]
    # Enforce correct dtypes to match target schema
    df = df.astype(target_dtypes)
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the exact same schema as the target,
# we perform a UNION (concatenation) of all source tables
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Write the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_65/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
